gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-khudawa: Noto Sans Khudawadi has rounds that stay unsealed, like a hook left unlatched, with capitals barely above the lowercase. Nulshock stretches wide above it in a single steady outline you could trace with a finger; try it larger than the body.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-kr: Noto Sans KR packs stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height, with curves that stay generous. Noto Sans KR keeps the text compact while Nulshock, stretched and spaced wide, draws neon-tube strokes that never change gauge.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-lao: Modern and tall-lettered, Noto Sans Lao keeps its mouths open. Over a long page, its high x-height makes lines feel full and easy to move through, while Nulshock's bent-tubing letters, all one gauge, stay up in the heading.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-lao-loo: Noto Sans Lao Looped makes words read as solid blocks rather than skylines, with bowls left unfinished on one side. And over a long stretch, that compact texture holds steady, while Nulshock keeps its flat, single-weight line for the heading.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Professional in manner, Noto Sans Lepcha has wide-opening curves and a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals. Nulshock does stretched display work, horizontals matching verticals; the sans handles the reading.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Approachable and tall-bodied, Noto Sans Limbu gapes open at every curve. Against Nulshock, whose stroke weight never varies and whose letters stretch wide, that open, upright body is what makes the pairing memorable.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Wide, wiry and technical up top. Nulshock draws one constant pen line across stretched capitals, and Noto Sans Lisu follows with tiny gaps under its ascenders and wide-open s curves for the sustained reading.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Nulshock stretches its letters wide and spaces them out, with curves that never thin. Noto Sans Lydian does the quieter job below, keeping capitals barely taller than lowercase and an opening like a sprung paper clip.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-mahajan: Modern and tall in the lowercase, Noto Sans Mahajani funnels wide throats into every e. Nulshock sits above it, stretched out with a constant pen-pressure look, so the heading and text feel clearly separate.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-malayal: Rope-like lines, stretched wide. Nulshock lays fine strands into its letters, and Noto Sans Malayalam lets the middle zone dominate each line, so a long page reads as a dense, steady texture.
